data: Restartable hydrogen upper-stage engine that sent Apollo translunar
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; NASA imagery.
The engine that sent Apollo to the Moon — twice

The J-2 burned hydrogen and oxygen, and it could restart in the vacuum of space — a capability that made Saturn V's trans-lunar injection burn possible. Rocketdyne's gas-generator design flew on Saturn V's second and third stages and on Saturn IB, combining performance with the in-space restarts that turned a launch vehicle into a true departure stage. It first flew in February 1966 and last flew on the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project in July 1975.
